facts.text: Florissant’s Cold Water Cemetery, the town’s first burial site from 1809, earned a National Register of Historic Places spot in 2004 for its social history.
An archaeological dig in Florissant uncovers 12,000 years of history, and a map shows the many historic sites visitors can explore.
Historic Florissant Inc. preserves the Gittemeier House, a 19th‑century home that now serves as the society’s headquarters.
Florissant boasts two celebrated historic residences: the Auguste Aubuchon House and the Lucy Patterson House, each reflecting Victorian elegance.
Louis, the settlement that would become Florissant, was officially founded in 1764 before adopting its current name.
The Shrine and Historic Site in Florissant houses four original buildings: a 1819 convent, 1821 church, 1840 rectory, and 1888 schoolhouse.
